answer: Each new identity starts as a bare kernel with no trust. To grow a pearl it must burn real fees on peer-verified useful work, and each new pearl layer costs quadratically more than the last — layer n costs n squared units — so reaching trusted status demands a steep, non-refundable sum. Pearls cannot be transferred, pooled, or split across clones, so k fakes pay the full curve k times. A yarrow lottery audits a random sample of pearls each epoch; a failed audit shatters the pearl and forfeits its burned fees, forcing the attacker to repay the whole quadratic curve again for every fake caught.
